function.name: find_beer
function.description: Recommend a beer based on specified attributes such as name, brewery, taste, aroma, color, style, and more. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

beer_name.description: The name of the beer to search for.

brewery.description: The brewery name to find similar beers.

taste.description: The desired taste profile in the beer, such as 'bitter', 'sweet', 'sour'.

aroma.description: The desired aroma profile in the beer, such as 'fruity', 'hoppy', 'malty'.

color.description: The desired color of the beer, such as 'pale', 'amber', 'dark'.

style.description: The style of beer being searched for, such as 'IPA', 'stout', 'lager'.

abv_min.description: The minimum alcohol by volume (ABV) percentage, typically a value under 12.5%. This is a float type value.

abv_max.description: The maximum alcohol by volume (ABV) percentage, a value logically above 0%. This is a float type value.

ibu_min.description: The minimum International Bitterness Units (IBU) score, typically a value under 120.

ibu_max.description: The maximum International Bitterness Units (IBU) score, logically above 0.

pairings.description: A list of food items to pair with the beer, such as 'burger', 'cheese', 'chocolate'.

message.content:
Sure! When pairing a dessert with Korean‑fried chicken, you’ll want something that balances the savory, spicy, and crispy flavors while offering a contrasting texture and sweetness. Here are three great options: | Dessert | Why It Works | |---------|--------------| | **Mango Sticky Rice** (Khao Niao Mamuang) | • Sweet coconut milk + ripe mango cuts through the saltiness.
• Soft glutinous rice provides a chewy contrast to crunchy chicken.
• Light enough not to overwhelm the palate after a hearty meal. | | **Sweet Red Bean Pancakes** (Pat Bunsik / Pat Tteokbokki) | • Mildly sweet red bean filling offers subtle earthiness.
• Thin pancake layers add a delicate crunch without competing with the chicken’s crispness.
• Traditional Korean flavor harmony keeps the theme consistent. | | **Chocolate Peanut Butter Cheesecake** | • Rich chocolate & nutty peanut butter counterbalance the spice.
• Creamy cheesecake smoothes out the heat from the chicken sauce.
• Slight bitterness of dark chocolate complements the umami notes of the dish. | ### Quick Pairing Tips 1. **Balance Heat:** If your chicken has a fiery kick, choose a sweeter dessert—mango sticky rice or a fruit-based sorbet works wonders. 2. **Texture Contrast:** Look for something either creamy or slightly chewy so it doesn’t compete with the crunch of the chicken. 3. **Flavor Harmony:** Keep the overall flavor palette cohesive – if you’re going for classic Korean vibes, stick with traditional sweets; otherwise, feel free to experiment with international twists! Pick one that fits your mood—or try all three over different meals—and enjoy a satisfying finish to your Korean fried chicken feast. Happy eating!
